Create an Adjacency Matrix of Gene Regulation with Propagation

get.gr.adj.Rd

This function generates an adjacency matrix from a gene regulatory network (gr.graph) with propagated regulatory effects. The propagation iteratively multiplies the adjacency matrix to capture higher-order regulatory interactions.

Usage

get.gr.adj(t = 2)

Arguments

t

An integer specifying the number of propagation steps. Default is 2. If t = 1, the function returns the direct adjacency matrix without propagation.

Value

A numeric adjacency matrix representing the propagated gene regulatory interactions. Each entry in the matrix reflects the weighted regulatory influence of a transcription factor (TF) on a target gene, adjusted by consensus stimulation and inhibition.

Details

The function starts by modifying the weights of gr.graph edges to reflect the regulatory effects. The edge weights are adjusted by multiplying the original weights with the difference between the indicator attributes consensus_stimulation and consensus_inhibition.

The resulting weighted adjacency matrix is then propagated by matrix multiplication for t steps to capture indirect regulatory interactions. Positive weights suggest stimulation effect, whereas negative weights indicate inhibition effect

See also

gr.graph

Examples

# Generate an adjacency matrix with the default 2-step propagation
get.gr.adj()
